- obligation: Startup recovery classification
- gap: No current startup coordinator opens/migrates/verifies the journal, rebuilds stale authoritative projections, acquires broker Layers, scans non-terminal transactions/expired leases, and classifies no-dispatch, dispatch-without-result, abort-in-progress, and terminal states before admission.
- original requiredChange (historical audit input; not current target): Implement the ordered startup state machine and open command admission only after all unfinished work has one durable classified next action.
- id: NOTE-12-1
- assessment: designed
- sourceEvidence:
  - services/uta/src/main.ts:63-87,104-128,145-176: current startup initializes managers/timers then exposes health/routes without journal classification
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/uta-manager.ts:63-71: account startup restores file state and callback persistence
  - historical architecture evidence pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64 (former lines 1239-1262): ordered recovery gate and per-account degraded reach
- currentBehavior: Startup restores available file history, starts snapshot/order timers and serves routes; it has no durable unfinished-work scan.
- problem: A boolean health response can be mistaken for safe command admission while old effects are unclassified; one unreachable broker must not indefinitely block unrelated accounts after local authority is valid.
- targetModel: StartupState = OwningHome|OpeningDatabase|Migrating|VerifyingJournal|RebuildingExecution|AcquiringConnections|ClassifyingRecovery(cursor,highWatermark)|Ready|Failed(evidenceRef). RuntimeHealth is Initializing|Recovering|Ready|Stopping|Failed with readiness evidence. Per-scope capability availability/reach and data stream lifecycle are separate tagged values over PublicScope or AccountScope; only controlled-effect aggregates require durable recovery classification before effect admission.
- pureTransitions:
  - classifyEffectRecovery(durableState,attempts) resumes preparation, preserves Prepared/AwaitingApproval for review/expiry only, requeues queued/no-start effects, observes started effects, resumes abort/compensation and retains RecoveryCase ownership
  - verifyReplay(records,highWatermark) checks effect schema/plan/projection versions before authority opens
  - admissionGate requires a durable next action/wait/recovery owner for each unfinished effect and emits Ready only after the local barrier
  - classifyCapabilityScope(scope,descriptor,availability) returns available/degraded/unavailable without changing descriptor identity
  - classifyDataStream(streamState) handles opening, gap, reconnect and end without creating an effect recovery case
- effectBoundary: effect-runtime sequences local startup and the writer records classification/projection checkpoints. Provider connections and data streams start as scoped resources; not every remote connection must be healthy for local authority or unrelated query scopes to be ready. Guardian consumes the tagged RuntimeHealth and scoped capability views.
- durability: Admission stays closed during effect journal replay/rebuild; replacement execution projections switch atomically. Classification jobs are typed and deduplicated. Data cursor/stream recovery follows provider replay/finality evidence; absence of replay is an explicit gap/degraded state, not a fabricated local sequence.
- errors:
  - JournalVerificationFailed(sequence,reason): close affected effect authority
  - ScopeConnectionUnavailable(scope,reach): degrade only the affected capability
  - RecoveryClassificationConflict(transactionId,version): reload/CAS
  - DataReplayUnavailable(scope,cursor): report gap/unavailable, do not infer complete history
- preservedBehavior:
  - One broken broker configuration does not stop non-trading Alice or independent available accounts
  - Keyless market-data scopes remain query-only and are never classified as executable trading accounts
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace health ok:true semantics with the RuntimeHealth union and local effect readiness gate
  - Retain stop handles for all effect/data workers and classify durable effect work before admission
  - Do not delete ephemeral source state before effect recovery decisions
  - Expose per-scope capability availability separately from startup and journal status
- verificationCases:
  - Kill during effect classification after half aggregates -&gt; next startup has one durable next action per aggregate and no early effect admission
  - Prepared/AwaitingApproval on restart -&gt; only expiry/review work exists; no forward effect dispatch before approval
  - One provider offline with a valid journal -&gt; unrelated scopes admit while that scope is degraded
  - An effect projection is corrupt but journal valid -&gt; deterministic rebuild before effect admission
  - A non-replayable data stream restarts -&gt; it reports a gap/degraded state without compensating or dispatching an order
- openQuestions: —
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: Startup/recovery barriers remain for local controlled-effect authority, but K02/K05 separate capability availability and data delivery from local readiness. An unavailable broker data scope must not block unrelated local effect or query scopes, while a corrupt effect journal still closes its authority.

The final target closes controlled-effect admission behind journal verification, projection rebuild and per-aggregate recovery classification, while scoped capability reach and data-stream lifecycle can degrade independently. Prepared/AwaitingApproval gets only review/expiry work, started work is observed, and keyless public data is never promoted to execution authority.

### NOTE-12-2

- chapter: 12
- note source (historical audit input; architecture references pinned to revision a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64): docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md:1293-1300

- obligation: Expected failure versus defect policy
- gap: Legacy code often converts corrupt persisted data or impossible states to empty/default values or generic errors; no owning-worker shutdown policy preserves diagnostic evidence.
- original requiredChange (historical audit input; not current target): Keep domain/broker/connection/conflict/unknown outcomes in typed failure channels, but treat malformed persisted records, impossible transitions, and broken schema invariants as defects that stop the affected worker/process and retain evidence.
- id: NOTE-12-2
- assessment: designed
- sourceEvidence:
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git-persistence.ts:28-39: all read/parse errors fall back then return undefined
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:147-153: thrown exceptions become broker rejected strings
  - services/uta/src/main.ts:179-189: shutdown swallows manager/event-log failures
  - historical architecture evidence pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64 (former lines 1293-1300): defects stop owner and preserve evidence
- currentBehavior: Corrupt persisted JSON can appear as empty history; unexpected execution errors are recorded as rejections.
- problem: Retry supervision after an impossible transition can repeat mutation, and silent defaults erase the evidence needed to classify old effects.
- targetModel: ExpectedFailure families are DomainRejection, ProviderRejection, ConnectionUnavailable, PreconditionConflict, OutcomeUnknown, StorageFailure, DeliveryGap and OutputViolation. Defects are PersistedCodecViolation, ReplayViolation, RelationalInvariantViolation and UnexpectedInterpreterDefect. SupervisionDecision = RetryReadAt|DegradeScope|StopWorkerPreserve|StopAuthorityPreserve; the decision is selected by boundary and phase, not a blanket catch. Data delivery defects isolate/pause the affected leaf; effect defects preserve evidence and mutation exclusion.
- pureTransitions:
  - classifyFailure(stage,typedFailure,durableBoundary) maps known no-send effect connection failure to rescheduling and possible-send failure to Unknown; pull/push delivery failure becomes gap/unavailable according to its contract
  - classifyDefect(owner,reach) stops global effect authority for journal/relational corruption or isolates malformed provider data while preserving any possible mutation reconcile gap
  - loadLegacyReadFailure distinguishes ENOENT from parse, permissions and IO errors; only genuine absence is absent history
  - classifyOutputViolation(capability,payload) rejects malformed data output and never silently returns empty state
- effectBoundary: Supervision observes typed causes, closes affected claim/admission gates and terminates pending replies. Provider stream code owns cancellation/reconnect; diagnostic sink failure cannot override effect journal truth. No blanket catch returns empty state or transforms a possible-send boundary into rejection.
- durability: A healthy writer records WorkerIncident/OutcomeUnknown before stopping effect work; a broken writer retains DB/WAL/raw evidence and reports the last durable sequence without claiming persistence. Data cursor gaps/violations retain delivery evidence and may degrade only that scope. Restart verifies and never clears corrupt state automatically.
- errors:
  - PersistedCodecViolation(path,recordId,schemaVersion): fatal effect-authority defect
  - NativeBoundaryMalformed(capability,evidenceRef): possible effect Unknown or data delivery isolation
  - WriterFailed(lastSequence): fail pending effect waiters with no memory/file bypass
  - StreamDeliveryFailure(resource,reason): typed end/pause/gap
- preservedBehavior:
  - Transient broker outages remain isolated rather than crashing every account
  - Expected user mistakes return actionable typed errors instead of stack traces
- replacementSteps:
  - Delete catch-all legacy load fallback on malformed/unreadable effect files
  - Remove throw-to-rejected conversion from controlled effect dispatch
  - Make supervision exhaustive by provider boundary, delivery mode and effect phase
  - Preserve data stream error/finality evidence without attaching order compensation to it
- verificationCases:
  - Corrupt persisted effect payload -&gt; startup fails closed with retained evidence, never empty history
  - Malformed provider response after possible effect send -&gt; Unknown, not ProviderRejected
  - Writer defect with queued effect callers -&gt; all resolve failure, none suspend forever
  - A data query timeout on one provider -&gt; unrelated effect/data workers remain live
- openQuestions: —
- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: The evidence-preserving failure boundary remains necessary. K07 adds provider protocol/delivery failures and K08 keeps possible-send Unknown distinct from known rejection; data-reader failures may be isolated without applying effect recovery semantics.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K05](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K07](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K11](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K12](../composition-contract.md)
- review: accepted — Source re-check: git-persistence.ts:27-39 collapses parse, permission and I/O failures into fallback/undefined; TradingGit.ts:147-153 converts thrown execution errors into rejected results; main.ts:179-189 swallows shutdown failures. The final target distinguishes expected provider/data failures from persisted/replay/relational/interpreter defects, preserves bytes and possible-send Unknown, isolates only the affected data leaf where safe, and never returns empty state or known rejection through a blanket catch.

- obligation: Required operational projections and metrics
- gap: Current health/log rows do not provide transactions by state/age, unknown outcomes awaiting reconciliation, RecoveryRequired residual exposure, durable queue lag/lease age, journal writer latency/backpressure, and projection checkpoint lag as typed operational views.
- original requiredChange (historical audit input; not current target): Add projection/query services and structured metrics for every listed view, keyed by transaction/step/dispatch/account/conflict/journal context and redacted by schema.
- id: NOTE-13-1
- assessment: designed

  - services/uta/src/main.ts:147-152: health reports only ok/startedAt/account count

  - detailed design D14: high-cardinality context must not become metric labels
- currentBehavior: Logs describe account polling, but no operational query identifies the age, ownership and residual of each unknown transaction.
- problem: A healthy socket counter cannot indicate stalled writer, stale projection or unresolved execution; putting transaction ids into metrics produces unbounded cardinality and may leak sensitive identities.
- targetModel: OperationalViews include effect TransactionsByStateAge, UnknownDispatches, RecoveryResiduals, DurableQueueLag, LeaseAge, WriterPressure and ProjectionLag, plus scoped CapabilityAvailability and DataDeliveryFreshness/cursor-gap views. ViewEnvelope(sequence,asOf,freshness,rows,nextCursor) is schema-bound. ExecutionContext is reserved for effect identity; DataContext carries provider/resource/cursor/finality. Metrics labels stay bounded; high-cardinality identities are redacted trace/log attributes.
- pureTransitions:
  - projectEffectOperational(event,state) updates state-entered time, unknown onset and recovery owner without resetting age
  - projectDataDelivery(frame,cursor) records freshness, finality, gap and provider identity without creating a dispatch context
  - computeLag(now,dueAt,checkpoint,head) returns duration/sequence gaps with clock uncertainty
  - redactDiagnostic(capabilitySchema,payload) preserves safe error references and rejects unknown/native secret fields
  - projectAvailability(descriptor,evidence) separates implementation/session/authorization availability from effect readiness
- effectBoundary: projection-store owns named SQL views/checkpoints; observability owns instrumentation/redaction/sinks; effect-runtime composes them. Operational readers authorize by the capability-declared PublicScope or AccountScope (with explicit subAccountId for account facts). Logs/metrics cannot authorize or schedule effects, and data diagnostics cannot be raw provider payloads.
- durability: Effect authority events retain correlation/timestamps and effect operational rows are queryable atomically. Data delivery checkpoints are independent and may be stale/incomplete. Writer latency instrumentation is ephemeral unless explicitly summarized; no history is fabricated across restart.
- errors:
  - ProjectionStale(checkpoint,head): expose lag, not empty rows
  - DiagnosticRedactionRejected(schema,field): drop unsafe diagnostic and count redaction error without changing effect
  - OperationalViewForbidden(scope): no cross-scope leak
  - CapabilityEvidenceUnavailable(capability): expose unavailable/degraded view
- preservedBehavior:
  - Human readable account/broker errors remain actionable but schema-redacted
  - Polling errors remain nonfatal when they are expected reach failures
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace health count as effect readiness with RuntimeHealth, capability availability and delivery freshness fields
  - Add paginated effect and data operational views without silently truncating unresolved residuals or stream gaps
  - Use low-cardinality labels and traces/exemplars for identity-rich context
  - Keep data finality/sequence provenance distinct from effect dispatch context
- verificationCases:
  - Repeated Unknown polls -&gt; firstUnknownAt stays fixed while nextDue advances
  - Read projection paused -&gt; response is visibly stale with head/checkpoint gap
  - Provider error includes a token -&gt; token never reaches diagnostics
  - A million effect transactions -&gt; metric series remain bounded
  - A stream loses cursor continuity -&gt; data view shows gap without creating an effect unknown
- openQuestions: —
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: Operational visibility remains required, but K05 introduces delivery freshness/cursor views alongside effect unknown/recovery views. K02/K06 require availability and schemas to be visible without turning transaction ids into metric labels or treating health as effect authorization.

The final target supplies schema-bound effect age/unknown/recovery/queue/lease/writer/projection views plus separately scoped capability and data freshness/gap views, keeps high-cardinality identity in redacted traces/logs, and does not let observability authorize or schedule an effect.

### NOTE-14-1

- chapter: 14
- note source (historical audit input; architecture references pinned to revision a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64): docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md:1331-1347
- note source paths: [docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md](https://github.com/mouriya-s-lab/OpenAlice/blob/a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64/docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md) (pinned historical revision a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64)
- obligation: Complete transaction-oriented public route set
- gap: No current target implementation provides POST /transactions, PUT /transactions/:id/draft, POST prepare/approve/reject/recover, GET transaction/events, GET /capabilities, or GET /accounts/:id/state with shared runtime schemas. Legacy wallet Git routes, no-op recovery, empty capability fallbacks, and manager/SDK state shapes are not target route implementations.
- original requiredChange (historical audit input; not current target): Add all ten application-owned transaction/capability/account routes listed in the architecture, with shared @traderalice/uta-protocol request/response/error schemas, durable admission semantics, and no database-row or broker-native payload exposure.
- id: NOTE-14-1
- assessment: designed
- sourceEvidence:
  - historical architecture evidence pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64 (former lines 1331-1347): exact ten transaction/capability/account routes
  - services/uta/src/http/routes-trading.ts:20-77,198-224: legacy loose schemas, one-shot pipeline and manager routes
  - detailed design D13: runtime schemas, error coverage and event pagination
- currentBehavior: Legacy routes operate on account instances and stringly order fields; one-shot status maps stage/commit/push rather than durable command acceptance.
- problem: Returning prepare success before a plan is durably compiled or exposing generic manager data makes client retry and approval ambiguous. Transport timeout is not transaction rejection.
- targetModel: UTA-facing transport exposes authenticated discovery/describe and application ports. Mutation-capable capability leaves use named command/receipt codecs with commandId and expectedVersion where an effect aggregate exists; read leaves use finite pull result schemas; push leaves use named stream frames, cancellation and end/error schemas. QueryCapabilities and account/scope views are fixed boundary projections, while provider command trees and extensions are descriptor-derived rather than a handwritten universal route table. Public data routes remain PublicScope; account/order routes require AccountScope and explicit subAccountId.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeRoute(route,capabilityDescriptor,wireInput) validates schema, path/body identity, scope and schema fingerprint before invoking a leaf
  - createOrReplacePrepareApproveRecover are available only for a composed controlled-effect leaf and return durable receipt/result variants
  - pull(capability,input) returns one finite validated page/result with cursor/completeness
  - push(capability,input,signal) returns typed frames and cancellation/end behavior; closing the client does not revoke an accepted effect
  - pageAuthorityEvents(scope,cursor,limit) returns stable sequence/nextCursor/end without hidden caps
- effectBoundary: HTTP/CLI is an outer interpreter: authenticate, discover/describe, decode, invoke application/reader, and encode. Provider bridge code handles native protocol; application/writer owns controlled-effect receipts. No route exposes SQL rows, SDK objects, functions, or credentials.
- durability: Controlled-effect responses emit only after receipt commit; retry uses the same commandId. Pull pages may be retried as finite reads under their cursor semantics; push cancellation releases only the stream resource. Read views expose freshness/availability and do not imply effect approval.
- errors:
  - ProtocolDecodeFailure(issues): typed boundary rejection
  - Unauthenticated/Forbidden: authentication/authorization failure before receipt disclosure
  - CapabilityNotFoundOrStale(identity,revision): no silent alternate semantics
  - VersionConflict/ApprovalMismatch/IdempotencyConflict: controlled-effect conflict
  - PrepareRejected(typedIssues): durable effect result, never fabricated Prepared
  - DeliveryUnavailableOrGap(capability,cursor): typed pull/push delivery result
- preservedBehavior:
  - One-shot UX can compose create/replace/prepare under policy but must expose durable waiting-for-approval
  - All legacy quantity/TP-SL/trailing/GTD/parent/OCA fields survive in named ADTs or fail explicit unsupported capability
- replacementSteps:
  - Derive provider help/CLI/route metadata from one capability declaration and fixed UTA boundary
  - Migrate Alice/CLI/connector calls together and delete old one-shot execution authority after cutover
  - Keep controlled-effect async prepare/approval distinct from data pull/push response lifecycles
  - Document unavailable structural leaves rather than adding unsupported handlers
- verificationCases:
  - Drop a controlled-effect response after commit and retry the same command id -&gt; one receipt returned
  - Preparation facts fail -&gt; durable typed PrepareRejected and no dispatch
  - Pull pagination over multiple pages -&gt; stable finite results with explicit completeness
  - Push client closes -&gt; stream ends/cancels its resource without canceling an already accepted effect
  - A capability tree without option/cancel leaf has no corresponding command/help node
- openQuestions: —
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: The route evidence remains about loose request/response and one-shot semantics, but K01/K02/K06 require route/help/call projections from capability declarations. Controlled-effect commands retain durable receipts; data pull/push routes expose their own schemas and lifecycle without universal transaction endpoints for every provider.

The final target keeps authenticated discovery/describe and descriptor-derived provider trees, uses command/receipt codecs and expected-version/digest checks only for composed controlled effects, and gives pull/push their own finite/stream schemas. Legacy quantity, TP/SL, trailing, TIF, parent/OCA semantics remain explicit or fail as structural capability absence rather than being hidden in a universal route table.

  - computeOperationalMetric(view) derives bounded aggregates without changing authority or delivery state
- effectBoundary: Adapters emit typed values to observability; domain does not acquire logger/time dependencies. Writer/scheduler enrich effect sequence/timing, while data adapters enrich frame/cursor facts. Observability is not journal or execution authority; sink finalization cannot settle or retry effects.
- durability: Effect audit facts remain in the effect journal; data cursor/finality facts remain in their delivery projection where required; view checkpoints belong to projection-store. Sink loss cannot lose receipts, authorize retries, or turn an incomplete data frame into a final one.

  - DataContextIncomplete(capability,cursor): preserve gap/finality uncertainty
- preservedBehavior:

  - Non-trading Alice remains outside UTA observability composition
- replacementSteps:

  - Move inline logs into typed ports as each source cuts over
  - Keep operational queries/checkpoints in projection-store
  - Require provider-specific redaction before raw native values reach sinks
- verificationCases:
  - Effect diagnostic cannot be built without step/scope/start sequence
  - Data-frame diagnostic includes cursor/finality but no transaction authority fields
  - Telemetry backend unavailable -&gt; effects still journal and data delivery reports its own status
  - Adapter raw native payload -&gt; boundary codec rejects secret/unknown fields
- openQuestions: —
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: The missing import boundary is real, but observability must cover both controlled effects and data delivery without making either a universal logger/telemetry registry. K03/K07 require typed redaction at provider boundaries and K05 requires frame/finality context.

  - Compensation fails permanently -&gt; RecoveryRequired retains keys/residual

- problem: A source install passing does not prove packaged native module ABI resolution, full WAL backup, relocation or corruption behavior. Project transfer excluding runtime identity is not automatically a safe trading-authority migration. A copied SQLite database can be internally consistent while being an arbitrary rollback or clone; databaseUuid, checksum, and journal high-watermark are audit metadata, not proof of sole ownership, freshness, or fencing of another host.
- targetModel: StorageAcceptanceCell(distribution:Source|Docker|PackagedDesktop,os,arch,nodeRuntimeAbi,sqliteVersion,packageArtifactDigest,homePath,scenario,status:Unexecuted|Unsupported|Passed|Failed) covers OpenMigrate, DurableEffectKillRecover, ConsistentBackupRestore, CompleteHomeRelocate, corruption, read-only and double-owner cases. RestoreMode = NormalRestart|RestoreQuarantine|ObservationOnly|AuthorityCutover; supported restore enters quarantine before effect admission and starts observation-only until external facts/ownership reconcile. Capability descriptors/schema fingerprints and provider bridge assets are part of the runtime cell evidence, not a claim that all providers are bundled.
- pureTransitions:
  - assessRestore(databaseIdentity,backupSequence,currentProviderEvidence) treats missing effect tail as Unknown risk; manifest metadata correlates evidence but cannot prove no rollback/clone/fence
  - enterRestoreQuarantine(restoreCase,sourceHome,destinationHome) records durable quarantine before admission; observation can reconcile provider facts, while AuthorityCutover requires old-owner stop/fence evidence
  - validateRelocation(sourceStopped,destinationOwnership,completeHome) requires no concurrent writers and correct credential references
  - matrixCoverage(releaseTargets,executedCells) leaves unexecuted cells Unexecuted/Unsupported and does not inherit support from another cell
  - validateRuntimeCapabilityCell(descriptor,wireSchema,bridgeAssets) rejects schema/ABI mismatch before exposing a leaf
- effectBoundary: Distribution jobs run the actual bundled entry; native SQLite remains external and is included in each UTA dependency closure/unpacked layout. Consistent backup uses SQLite backup API or stopped complete-home copy. Provider bridges decode exact schemas at runtime. Raw copies bypassing quarantine are not claimed safe or detectable.
- durability: Database UUID/schema/checksum/high-watermark are audit correlation only, never sole-writer, rollback or exactly-once proof. Restore does not overwrite a live effect authority; observation-only startup reconciles current provider facts before explicit cutover. Unexecuted cells cannot enter effect Ready. Data cache/stream state remains subject to its own replay/finality evidence after restore.
- errors:
  - NativeSqliteLoadFailure(runtimeAbi,artifact): no fallback storage
  - RestoreQuarantineRequired(restoreCase): no effect admission before quarantine
  - BackupAuthorityStale(sequence): observation-only restore
  - HomeOwnershipUnproven(path): refuse authority cutover
  - CorruptJournal(recordRef): fail closed without reset
  - DistributionCellUnexecuted(cell): no Ready/support claim
  - RuntimeCapabilitySchemaMismatch(capability): do not expose the leaf
- preservedBehavior:
  - Docker retains independent UTA dependency closure and optional broker-pack separation
  - Data root remains portable complete home
  - Non-trading Alice can still run when UTA native driver is unavailable
  - Manifest/package metadata alone does not upgrade an unexecuted distribution cell or native ABI claim
- replacementSteps:
  - Add the selected SQLite stack to UTA production closure while preserving native externalization
  - Extend desktop/Docker packaging acceptance to the actual UTA runtime and capability bridge assets
  - Add durable trading-authority restore/cutover gates; never auto-activate a clone
  - Keep ordinary same-home restart distinct from restore/relocation
  - Record every release cell and provider capability evidence before support claims
- verificationCases:
  - Packaged runtime opens/migrates a relocated complete home and executes a durable mock effect
  - Backup before provider fill, restore after fill -&gt; observation-only detects current fact and no effect dispatch before cutover
  - Valid checksum with arbitrary rollback/clone -&gt; quarantine remains
  - Wrong native ABI -&gt; startup failure and no JSON fallback
  - Unexecuted OS/architecture/provider bridge cell -&gt; status remains Unexecuted/Unsupported and no effect Ready
- openQuestions:

- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: Packaging/native ABI evidence and restore quarantine remain empirical gates. The corrected target additionally requires each distribution to carry the same fixed UTA-facing capability/schema boundary while preserving provider-native internals and keeping restore/data observation distinct from effect authority.

The final target requires per-distribution/OS/architecture/runtime/bridge evidence for native open/migrate, durable kill/recover, backup/restore, relocation, corruption, read-only and double-owner cases; restore enters RestoreQuarantine and ObservationOnly before cutover. - chapter: 19
- note source (historical audit input; architecture references pinned to revision a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64): docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md:1474-1489
- note source paths: [docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md](https://github.com/mouriya-s-lab/OpenAlice/blob/a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64/docs/uta-effect-runtime-architecture.md) (pinned historical revision a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64)
- obligation: No process-external database, queue, or workflow requirement
- gap: Existing SQLite/scheduler recommendations do not explicitly forbid introducing an external database, durable queue, or workflow service as a runtime prerequisite.
- original requiredChange (historical audit input; not current target): Keep UTA self-contained with embedded SQLite and in-process Effect runtime; external infrastructure may not become required execution authority or recovery state.
- id: NOTE-19-1
- assessment: designed
- sourceEvidence:
  - historical architecture evidence pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64 (former lines 1474-1489): forbids external authority stores/workflow engines and blind retries
  - services/uta/src/main.ts:63-168: current UTA process owns managers, poller, FX, snapshots and HTTP
  - Dockerfile:107-137,143-170: co-located UTA process and persistent home, not an external database prerequisite
- currentBehavior: UTA is a co-located service with local state and optional brokers; adding durability does not require a new infrastructure service.
- problem: Delegating scheduler/history to Redis/Postgres/workflow service would create deployment and recovery dependencies outside the chosen home and split execution authority.
- targetModel: RuntimeAuthoritySet is one UTA process/home with embedded effect journal, capability registry/availability evidence and in-process effect workers. ExternalDependencyRole = ProviderEffectEndpoint|ProviderDataFacts|MarketDataStream|OptionalTelemetrySink|OptionalBackupDestination; none holds sole approval/recovery authority. DurableIntent is a schema-bound provider-declaration-derived controlled-effect record with only small local lifecycle tags, not a closed global taxonomy. Data pulls/pushes are declaration-derived resources over PublicScope or AccountScope as declared, with independent lifecycle.
- pureTransitions:
  - checkRuntimeRequirements(config) rejects a mandatory external queue/database/workflow authority for effect acceptance or recovery
  - degradeOptionalSink(availability) affects telemetry/export only, never effect journal readiness
  - recoverOfflineLocal(effectJournal) classifies unfinished effects locally while provider observations wait durably
  - composeProviderResource(descriptor,scope) records data/effect availability for the declared PublicScope or AccountScope without turning external reach into approval or inventing account identity
- effectBoundary: Only provider effect/data facts and optional sinks are remotely required for the relevant capability. Local scheduler scans embedded authority; timers/queues are hints. Provider data streams are resource-scoped and may be unavailable without creating an external workflow authority.
- durability: Approvals, controlled-effect jobs, locks, receipts, reconciliation cursors and recovery owners remain in the same home. Data cursor/checkpoint records may be local or provider-backed only as declared, but no external acknowledgement substitutes for local effect commit. Complete-home backup contains local recovery authority.
- errors:
  - UnsupportedExternalAuthority(dependency,role): configuration rejected
  - OptionalExportUnavailable(destination): expose lag without blocking effect journaling
  - ProviderFactsUnavailable(scope): durable waiting/degraded capability, not workflow fallback
  - DataStreamUnavailable(scope,reason): typed unavailable/degraded result
- preservedBehavior:
  - UTA remains optional for non-trading users and deployable with the existing local/Docker process topology
  - Broker facts remain remote authority; embedded SQLite does not pretend to own venue state
- replacementSteps:
  - Implement finite typed effect handlers and provider data leaves alongside each executable slice, not a generic workflow engine
  - Reject mandatory external state dependencies during composition review
  - Keep telemetry/backup as optional projections of local truth
  - Keep remote provider facts as evidence sources rather than authority for approval/recovery

Loopback is the only interprocess trust assumption.
- problem: A host-local caller can bypass Alice presentation guards; a connector status check or client-supplied actor is not authorization for the plan eventually executed. The enabled AI path is an existing explicit capability, but its current boolean gate is outside UTA and does not durably bind actor, scope, revision, digest, policy version, and expiry. Configuration replacement and process restart have no transaction/recovery ownership fence.
- targetModel: AuthenticatedAliceRequest contains service audience, home identity, principal, workspace/session correlation, granted actor role, commandId, canonical body digest, issuedAt/expiresAt and proof. UTA resolves the capability-declared PublicScope or AccountScope and selects a declaration-derived capability leaf; only a controlled effect is wrapped with an ApprovalBinding. ExecutionApproval = ManualApproval | ConfiguredAutoApproval(actor,scope,revision,planDigest,policyVersion,expiresAt). AccountLifecycleCapability accepts Configure/RotateCredentialReference/Disable/Retire with expectedConfigRevision and never exposes raw broker access. The source allowAiTrading setting is an authorized product-policy input, not a self-authorizing body boolean.

  - retireAccount(configRevision, unfinishedEffects) disables new effect admission and either retains recovery-only access or permits credential retirement after remote liabilities are classified
- effectBoundary: Alice authenticates the human or configured service actor and carries a short-lived proof over the private boundary; Guardian-provisioned key material remains in the existing secret/runtime path. UTA verifies proof, resolves credential references, and owns capability/lifecycle effects. Alice receives descriptors, credential references, and masked views; data reads and streams require resource authorization but not order approval.
- durability: CommandReceipts deduplicate by principal scope and commandId after authentication. Approval events bind effect capability identity, transaction/revision/digest, actor, policy and expiry atomically with jobs. Configuration records a desired revision and credential-reference write intent, applies it idempotently, then marks the revision available; no secret enters plans, receipts, or public views.

  - CredentialReferenceUnavailable(reference): degrade the affected capability without logging secret
- preservedBehavior:

  - Account id remains stable across credential rotation
  - allowAiTrading=false remains an AwaitingApproval/manual Web UI path; explicit enabled policy retains the source auto-push capability only as a UTA-authorized auto-approval binding
  - Lite/read-only presentation and connector hidden-operation warnings remain explicit
- replacementSteps:

  - Translate tradingPush and connector approval into revision/digest approval bindings; enabled policy calls UTA approval rather than a raw push path
  - Strip untrusted actor headers at the BFF and require authenticated assertions on non-health capability routes

  - allowAiTrading disabled -&gt; effect request remains AwaitingApproval with no dispatch; enabled policy -&gt; one digest-bound approval reaches writer commit and DispatchStarted, never a direct broker call
  - Credential rotation with an Unknown effect -&gt; new writes are disabled while scoped observation remains available

- problem: A compensator built as a callback or finalizer loses both its applied-effect basis and its dispatch identity; retry can open an additional economic position.
- targetModel: ObservationJob is a provider-declared pull or resource-scoped push lifecycle with a serializable PublicScope or AccountScope (including explicit subAccountId when account facts require it), cursor/stream identity, completeness and recovery facts. CompensationProgram is a separate controlled-effect record bound to applied evidence, a source effect revision, restoration target, dependency edges and approved risk limits. Durable job targets are typed data-observation, preparation/expiry, forward-effect, or compensation identities; no callback/closure is persisted and no data frame is put through order approval.
- pureTransitions:
  - advanceObservation(streamOrPull, frameOrPage) updates cursor, completeness, gap and next-due state without creating an order transaction
  - planAbort(progress, acceptedPolicy, appliedFacts) supersedes unstarted forward effect jobs, then returns AwaitConclusiveOutcomes or a compensation dependency DAG
  - nextCompensation(frontier, observedResults) selects only nodes whose dependencies settled and recalculates economic residuals from confirmed facts
  - observeCompensation(outcome, target) produces Restored, ContinueObserving or RecoveryRequired; an unknown compensation is observed, not recursively mutated
- effectBoundary: A provider adapter owns data subscription resources and decodes native frames; the scheduler owns durable observation cursors and invokes the narrow effect dispatch port only for persisted compensation steps. Reconnect can resume a stream cursor when the provider declares that ability, but cannot resume a business effect by itself.
- durability: Data observations persist only the evidence, cursor, completeness and recovery state required by their delivery contract. Abort, supersession and compensation plans commit through the effect writer with DispatchStarted/epoch and evidence ingestion; observation completion and its next cursor are one writer decision where durable persistence is required.
- errors:
  - ObservationGap(scope,cursor): pause or mark incomplete according to the provider stream contract
  - AppliedOutcomeIndeterminate(dispatchIds): reconcile before compensation
  - CompensationBudgetExceeded(actual,authorized): stop and retain a recovery case
  - RestorationUnavailable(reason,evidence): no improvised inverse effect
- preservedBehavior:
  - An unhealthy broker does not stop unrelated account observations
  - Idle accounts do not repeatedly query known-empty pending books; scheduled external observation remains distinct
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace tick counters as effect authority with typed observation cursors and durable next-due facts
  - Keep pull/push data delivery out of order prepare/approve/compensate paths
  - Introduce compensation only through persisted controlled-effect steps, never legacy push/placeOrder from an abort handler
  - Retain observation after an accepted effect while working external resources remain, using provider-declared scope and freshness
- verificationCases:
  - A push stream disconnect with a declared replay cursor resumes or reports a gap without creating an approval
  - Kill after compensation venue acceptance but before ack persistence -&gt; restart observes the original effect identity and never submits a new inverse
  - Two effect steps with a dependency edge -&gt; dependent restoration is selected only after prerequisite facts settle
  - Unknown forward fill quantity -&gt; no compensation quantity is guessed

- obligation: Effect Queue boundary
- gap: No current facility implements Queue as bounded admission/worker wake-up while durable jobs remain authoritative in SQLite. Legacy queues and Promise chains either lack capacity or durability separation.
- original requiredChange (historical audit input; not current target): Use a configured-capacity Effect Queue only for admission/wake-up, block producers at capacity, and persist EffectJob identity before any broker mutation. Never present the Queue as the authoritative job store.
- id: NOTE-4-1
- assessment: designed
- sourceEvidence:
  - historical architecture evidence pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64 (former lines 920-951): bounded writer queue, take/drain group commit and post-commit Deferred
  - composition-contract.md K01/K03/K08; transaction-contract.md §6: closed effect commands, grouped failures and cancellation boundary
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:171-179: persistence occurs after memory commit/head mutation
- currentBehavior: Current execution has a per-instance inflight boolean, not a bounded process-wide durable admission service.
- problem: A naive queue implementation can acknowledge before commit, drop blocked callers, deadlock outcome ingestion behind new admission, or evaluate conflicting commands against the same pre-batch state.
- targetModel: WriterEnvelope(commandId,principalScope,payloadDigest,EffectWriteCommand,replyDeferred) carries only commands that change local effect authority or an effect-owned projection checkpoint. EffectWriteCommand is a small local safety ADT composed by the application; provider leaves supply their own exact input/output/error codecs and are not forced into a global handler union. Provider data delivery checkpoints remain with their own resource owner outside the effect writer. User admission and internal-progress ingress are separately bounded and served by one writer. Data pulls return finite validated results and push streams use bounded, declared backpressure/cancellation resources outside the effect writer.
- pureTransitions:
  - formBatch(first, currentlyAvailableSnapshot) drains a finite snapshot of each configured effect queue and never follows newly arriving producers indefinitely
  - applyBatch(stagedDatabaseState, envelopes) processes FIFO within each lane and deterministic fair lane order; each accepted command updates the staged state seen by the next command
  - resolveDuplicate(storedReceipt,digest) returns the original result or IdempotencyConflict; a domain rejection is a result and does not abort unrelated siblings
  - admitDelivery(resource,capacity,policy) returns a typed backpressure or cancellation decision for a data stream without manufacturing an effect receipt
- effectBoundary: Queue/Deferred are transport to the sole JournalWriter fiber for durable effect decisions. Data provider adapters own stream buffers and pull cancellation; scheduler wakeups only prompt durable eligibility scans. No provider IO occurs while the local effect SQL transaction is open.
- durability: The writer begins one SQL transaction, resolves effect receipts and staged state sequentially, appends accepted events/jobs/locks, commits, then completes replies. SQL failure rolls the batch back; an admitted cancellation does not erase intent. Data delivery may persist cursor/checkpoint facts according to its own contract, never an order WAL per frame.
- errors:
  - WriterUnavailable(lifecycle): do not enqueue a durable effect
  - StorageFailure(operation,sqliteCode): rolled-back callers receive retry-same-command guidance
  - CommitOutcomeIndeterminate(commandIds): reopen/query receipts before any effect dispatch
  - WriterDefect(evidenceRef): close effect lanes and complete pending waiters
  - DeliveryBackpressure(resource,capacity): apply declared stream policy rather than dropping a trading command
- preservedBehavior:
  - Callers still receive explicit per-command errors; one business conflict must not reject unrelated commands
  - No silent batch-size truncation; configured queue capacities remain visible
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace onCommit persistence permission with writer receipt-only effect dispatch authorization
  - Keep finite sequential staged-state decisions for effect commands without introducing a global provider switch
  - Keep accepted receipt constructors private and remove detached persistence from effect execution
  - Give each data pull/push capability an explicit finite-result or stream-lifecycle resource policy
- verificationCases:
  - Two same-version effect edits in one batch -&gt; first accepted, second VersionConflict, both receipts durable
  - SQL fails on final effect row -&gt; no earlier effect receipt or broker permission
  - Fill progress arrives while user effect admission is full -&gt; internal progress advances without lost evidence or unbounded queue
  - A push stream exceeds its declared buffer -&gt; its typed overflow policy fires and no order receipt is fabricated

- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: The post-commit and bounded-admission finding remains valid for durable controlled effects, but K01/K02 reject a universal provider command product. The writer handles declaration-derived effect/application commands and progress records; pull results and push frames use their own finite delivery resources.

  - beginPrepare(draft, expectedVersion) freezes a serializable controlled-effect revision and refuses unsaved candidate data
  - advanceDataCursor(cursor, delivery) accepts only provider-declared sequence/cursor transitions and marks a gap rather than silently replaying an old frame
- effectBoundary: The application may use STM/TRef for local views and provider-local caches, but submits effect Draft changes to the writer. Hydration uses named readers; prepare never trusts an arbitrary cache. Data stream cancellation and cache eviction release only that delivery resource and cannot alter a saved effect revision.
- durability: Only a committed writer receipt makes a controlled-effect edit saved; PrepareStarted and its revision are durable before fact reads. Cache loss discards unsaved UI edits or data pages only. Retirement of a prepared effect uses a no-start CAS and creates a new draft revision; a data cursor checkpoint does not retire or approve an effect.
- errors:

  - UnsavedProposal(editSequence): save candidate before effect preparation

  - Editing an approved/prepared plan requires reapproval rather than mutating queued work

  - Invalidate local views by writer version or provider cursor, not elapsed time alone
  - Use STM only where multiple local references need atomic view updates; do not add a mandatory store
  - Keep data reader/stream state separate from effect revision and approval lifecycle
- verificationCases:
  - Restart after a saved effect ReplaceDraft receipt -&gt; same draft restores without TRef state
  - Concurrent local edit and prepare -&gt; prepared digest binds one committed schema revision
  - Expire a prepared effect that has DispatchStarted -&gt; retirement refused
  - Evict a data cache during a push stream -&gt; no effect revision or approval changes

- currentBehavior: A pushed batch gathers heterogeneous results without a replayable transaction-state event transition model.
- problem: The baseline Decision cannot represent a duplicate without emitting fake facts; its state payloads lose plan/progress during reconciliation. State/event completeness must cover initial creation, draft edits, approvals, dispatch, rejection, compensation and recovery.
- targetModel: EffectDecision = Rejected(DomainFailure) | Unchanged(ReceiptRef) | Accepted(NonEmpty&lt;EffectEvent&gt;,DurableIntent[]).   - decideEffect(state,command,facts,now,allocatedIds) exhaustively selects a transition without IO, clock reads, or id generation
  - evolveEffect(state,event) requires aggregate identity and contiguous version before applying a legal lifecycle transition
  - reduceEvidence(progress,evidence) deduplicates native identities and correction revisions rather than adding duplicate callbacks
  - foldBatchSettled(perStep) records conclusively settled independent effect outcomes without claiming all succeeded
  - reduceDataDelivery(cursor,frame) handles provider sequence/finality/gap rules independently of effect state
- effectBoundary: Application gathers typed facts from provider leaves; the effect writer reloads authority and calls pure effect decisions inside its transaction. Provider decoders reject unknown persisted/schema versions at their boundary. Data replay has its own cursor and resource lifecycle; neither evaluator performs network IO.
- durability: Creation, draft, preparation, approval, dispatch-start, observation, abort, compensation, settlement and recovery events are complete for effects; infrastructure-only jobs have their own typed owner. Duplicate accepted commands return the original receipt. Data evidence/checkpoints are durable only when their delivery or later decision contract requires them and never fake an effect event.
- errors:
  - InvalidCommandState(state,command): durable effect-domain rejection receipt
  - ReplayViolation(sequence,expectedState,eventTag): stop affected authority and preserve bytes
  - EvidenceIdentityConflict(nativeEventId,digests): quarantine contradictory evidence
  - DataDeliverySchemaViolation(capability,frame): terminate or pause that stream without classifying it as an effect rejection
- preservedBehavior:

  - Committed at acceptance continues independent order observation without reopening its historical criterion
- replacementSteps:

  - Replace generic success booleans with typed per-capability results and per-effect step results
  - Remove catch-all evolution defaults while preserving PlanRef/ProgressRef in active effect states
  - Keep provider pull/push delivery schemas and finality independent of effect event replay
- verificationCases:
  - Replay every effect lifecycle variant through legal events -&gt; same state as live writer
  - Duplicate accepted effect command -&gt; original receipt and no added event/version
  - Independent rejected and accepted effect leaves -&gt; BatchSettled reports both, never AllSucceeded
  - A duplicate data callback is idempotent by provider identity and does not create an effect event
  - A later fill correction updates projections but does not rewrite a historical effect criterion

- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: Replayable state/event completeness is still necessary for controlled effects and their recovery. The corrected boundary limits the finite lifecycle ADT to those effects; provider data results/frames and catalog/cache projections are not forced into transaction states.

CompensationIntent is serializable and binds a source effect, applied evidence, allowed class, target and compiler version. A provider-owned pure compensation compiler consumes resolved facts; NativeConformanceRecord is per provider capability leaf and effect variant, not a global broker promise. Missing evidence is NativeGuaranteeUnproven.
- pureTransitions:

  - compileAppliedCompensation(intent,actualAppliedFacts,currentFacts) recalculates residual cancellation or exposure restoration; unknown fills return NeedsObservation
  - validateRestoration(result,declaredDomain) checks each identity/state/economic predicate and never upgrades a class because a call returned success
  - admitNativeConformance(leaf,record) permits only the specifically evidenced retry/restoration behavior; absent scope, horizon, lookup, absence or sender-fence evidence remains unavailable
- effectBoundary: Provider adapter performs mutation IO only from persisted compensation steps and receives sealed credentials at dispatch. The effect kernel authorizes risk and records evidence; a provider-owned compiler remains pure after fact collection. Data pull/push adapters do not compile inverse effects.
- durability: Assessment, assumptions and consent are immutable effect plan data. Each compensation program binds an applied-evidence digest and unique source-abort identity; its dispatch identity and observations use the normal started/unknown protocol. NativeConformanceRecord stores evidence version, identity scope, horizon and lookup/absence/fencing limits; absence leaves Unknown/RecoveryRequired.

  - CompensationAssumptionInvalidated(fact): observe/recover, do not use stale undo
  - EconomicLimitExceeded(requested,remainingBudget): stop before further risk
  - NativeConformanceMissing(capability,evidenceGaps): safe retry and Exact restoration remain unavailable
- preservedBehavior:
  - Partial-close quantity is checked against observed exposure
  - Cancel and replace never advertises Exact when venue identity/priority changes
  - Mock reversible-ledger behavior and SDK method presence never upgrade a real adapter's compensation or idempotency class
- replacementSteps:
  - Keep runtime functions out of prepared/public schemas; persist only serializable assessment and intent
  - Grant Exact only where a provider capability has explicit restoration-domain proof
  - Record fee/slippage/identity-loss evidence for state-restoring or economic classes
  - Require evidence per provider leaf before granting safe retry, absence, or Exact claims; retain this entry as empirical-retained
- verificationCases:

  - Restored quantity with a changed native identity -&gt; cannot satisfy identity-preserving Exact
  - Economic undo exceeds approved limits -&gt; no compensating effect is sent and residual is exposed
  - No provider/action conformance record -&gt; post-start timeout remains Unknown with an observation job
  - A paused sender can resume after lease expiry -&gt; missing fence keeps the original identity in RecoveryRequired
- openQuestions:
  - Which real broker/action combinations have empirically proven restoration and idempotency guarantees remains adapter-specific acceptance evidence; unproven capabilities are unavailable, not assumed.
- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: The empirical gap and the durable distinction between assessment and runtime compiler remain fully applicable to controlled effects. Under K07/K08 each provider effect leaf owns its conformance evidence; no universal action map or native guarantee is inferred for other leaves, and data readers never receive compensation machinery.

  - admitDataResource(resource,quota) returns available/degraded/backpressured without acquiring an effect lock

Provider data adapters acquire/release stream resources under their own declared scope and quota; external/manual activity is observed, not locally locked as an effect.
- durability: Complete effect conflict sets enter prepared plan digests and job rows; plan locks and run permits are atomic. Data subscription identity/cursor may be checkpointed, but loss or cancellation does not release an unresolved effect lock or alter effect reservations.

  - Remove the per-account boolean as exclusion authority
  - Add risk reservations instead of broad account locking for every effect
  - Define provider data resource keys and quotas separately from effect conflicts

  - Opposite key-order multi-scope effects -&gt; no partial lock/deadlock
  - Different instruments share a connection -&gt; concurrent effect dispatch up to declared capacity

  - Two streams on one feed exceed quota -&gt; one is backpressured while unrelated effect locks remain unchanged

- obligation: Atomic lease acquisition and dispatch-boundary recovery
- gap: No current worker atomically selects eligible unleased work, stamps owner/expiry, appends JobClaimed, commits, and then executes. Restart cannot distinguish reclaim from work that crossed dispatch.

  - transaction-contract.md §7: explicit started boundary and stale-worker limitation

- currentBehavior: No durable boundary distinguishes a claimed but unsent operation from a broker-accepted operation whose response was lost.
- problem: Lease expiration fences local writes but cannot revoke a paused worker's network call. Reclaiming as fresh dispatch after a possible send creates duplicate economic effects.
- targetModel: EffectJobLease = Ready(notBefore)|Leased(ownerInstanceId,epoch,deadline)|Completed(resultRef)|Failed(failureRef), with monotonic leaseEpoch. EffectAttempt = Planned(identity)|DispatchStarted(identity,owner,epoch,startSequence)|Acknowledged(ackRef)|Rejected(rejectionRef)|Unknown(evidenceRef). A data push has a separate StreamLifecycle = Opening|Live(cursor)|Paused(gap)|Ended(reason)|Failed(error) and does not create DispatchStarted unless it is itself a controlled mutation capability.
- pureTransitions:
  - claimEligible(now,effectJob,permits,budget) checks dependencies/conflicts/capacity and increments epoch
  - startEffect(job,epoch,plan,latestPreconditions,now) CAS-checks live lease/approval/plan and appends DispatchStarted before provider mutation
  - classifyExpiredAttempt selects unsent reclaim only when no start boundary exists; any started effect selects ObserveUnknown
  - ingestLateEvidence validates provider identity independently of stale scheduling ownership; stale workers cannot complete/requeue or allocate a new effect
  - advanceStream(stream,frame) follows provider cursor/sequence/finality rules and marks gap/ended without invoking effect retry
- effectBoundary: The writer commits effect claim and start separately; scheduler invokes provider mutation only after the committed start receipt. Adapters do not automatic-retry mutation. Data stream adapters own cancellation and reconnect within their declared contract and cannot authorize an effect.
- durability: Effect claims, permits, starts, observations and unknown reservations are durable; remote retry requires verified provider identity/horizon or conclusive absence plus old-sender fencing. Stream cursor/checkpoint persistence records delivery state only and does not grant resend or effect permission.

  - RetryNotProven(identity,evidenceGap): remain Unknown/RecoveryRequired
  - ConnectionGenerationChanged(expected,actual): revalidate before new effect start
  - StreamCursorGap(resource,cursor): pause or end stream according to provider contract
- preservedBehavior:
  - Connection recovery is independent and may continue for unrelated accounts
  - Valid late broker facts are not discarded merely because a worker lease expired
- replacementSteps:
  - Keep the DispatchStarted receipt/epoch CAS barrier in controlled effects
  - Remove timer-driven effect mutation retries and separate stale evidence ingestion from stale owner completion
  - Specify each push stream cancellation/reconnect/finality contract independently
  - Do not call a data-frame acknowledgement a remote effect acknowledgement
- verificationCases:
  - Kill after effect claim before start -&gt; unsent effect can be reclaimed
  - Pause after effect start before socket send, expire lease, resume old worker -&gt; no second sender
  - Late ack from old effect epoch -&gt; evidence stored once but old worker cannot complete new job
  - A first-page empty data listing -&gt; stream remains incomplete and does not authorize effect resend
  - SIGINT closes a push stream while a previously accepted effect remains unchanged

- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: The durable start boundary, stale-worker fencing, and Unknown classification remain exactly the required safety behavior for controlled effects. ### NOTE-9-1

- chapter: 9

- obligation: Complete broker service-provider interface
- gap: Current adapters expose legacy Promise-based IBroker objects, mutable connection state, direct mutations, static capability arrays, and ad hoc observation. - id: NOTE-9-1
- assessment: blocked-on-evidence
- sourceEvidence:
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:180-205: Promise&lt;unknown&gt; dispatcher and guard pipeline
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/brokers/types.ts:1-7: legacy broker types re-export public package
  - historical architecture evidence pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64 (former lines 1121-1185): scoped connection, interpreter, outcome and contextual capability requirements
  - composition-contract.md K07/K08/K11: deterministic native compilation and native evidence limits
  - Alpaca provider design: client identity and broker idempotency/child-group evidence remain acceptance facts
  - CcxtCore provider design: Unknown is RecoveryRequired and native idempotency evidence is not established
  - CcxtVenues provider design: timeout requires observation and venue coverage; partial listings are not absence
  - Ibkr provider design: lookup scope and native idempotency remain unproven
  - Longbridge provider design: post-dispatch Unknown and native absence/idempotency remain open
- currentBehavior: UnifiedTradingAccount calls one generic broker interface directly and receives erased mutation results; public broker types are coupled through a compatibility re-export.
- problem: An interpreter whose Action/Ack/Observation generics widen independently can return an observation for the wrong action. Runtime availability must not serialize Schema or functions into a plan or client response.
- targetModel: Each provider instance declares a capability tree of exact leaves: input schema, result schema, domain-error schema, delivery mode, effect category, resources, availability evidence and provider extension fields. CapabilityDescriptor is the fixed UTA-facing envelope; provider internals may be SDK/classes/REST/OpenAPI/another process. Scope is PublicScope or AccountScope as the leaf declares; account/order facts require AccountScope and an explicit subAccountId when the provider distinguishes wallets, while public Candle/Instrument/News leaves do not invent an account. Order, Candle, Instrument, News and NewsGroup are semantic units with provider-declared exact extensions, not a universal action map. withTransaction composes only a mutating leaf and preserves its precise schema/error/resource types; no absent leaf is represented by an Unsupported handler.
- pureTransitions:
  - declareCapability(provider,leafSchema,handler,resources) derives descriptor, validation, help and metadata from one declaration
  - composeEffectCapability(leaf,transactionPolicy) adds prepare/approval/dispatch/recovery only when the leaf has an external effect and preserves provider-declared native fields and legal combinations without widening to a generic object
  - deriveAvailability(instance,scope,implementation,session,authorization) reports Available, Unavailable or Degraded separately from schema identity; scope is PublicScope or AccountScope as declared, never inferred from reachability
  - decodeNative(leaf,nativePayload) validates provider-specific response/error evidence at the adapter boundary and returns a typed protocol failure or exact leaf result
  - bindInvocation(discoveryRevision,capabilityIdentity,schemaFingerprint) rejects stale/revoked capability identity instead of silently selecting another leaf
- effectBoundary: The bridge exposes version negotiation, discovery, correlated request/response or stream and cancellation at the UTA-facing boundary. Provider adapter code owns native lookup, SDK lifecycle, subscriptions and decoding. Only a composed controlled-effect leaf receives the scheduler dispatch port; read/pull/push leaves are resource-scoped data operations and cannot authorize transactions.
- durability: Persist descriptor identity/fingerprint/revision, availability evidence and serializable effect plans as needed; never persist functions, runtime Schema objects, SDK classes or secrets. Effect dispatch identity/unknown/recovery use the durable protocol. Data cursors/frames retain provider identity/finality/gap facts without order WAL or compensation records.
- errors:
  - CapabilityNameConflict(provider,identity): reject load, never last-write-wins
  - SchemaFingerprintMismatch(expected,observed): reject invocation
  - CapabilityUnavailable(reason): preserve identity but refuse execution
  - NativeProtocolViolation(capability,evidenceRef): classify possible effect mutation as Unknown
  - OutputSchemaViolation(capability,evidenceRef): reject data output or isolate effect worker according to delivery/effect boundary
- preservedBehavior:
  - All existing order-entry features remain represented and receive explicit capability decisions
  - Connection-specific health is preserved without embedding transaction state in the connection
  - Unproven SDK/mock outcomes, empty listings and transport acknowledgements never become native capability evidence
- replacementSteps:
  - Keep the existing IBroker/global-switch path as source evidence only and introduce a declaration-derived provider adapter boundary
  - Migrate one provider capability leaf through discovery, exact schema validation, availability, invocation and observation before removing its old mutation path
  - Let each provider preserve native parameters/extensions and report missing leaves structurally
  - Require conformance evidence per effect leaf before granting safe retry, absence or compensation; do not add empty handlers for other providers
- verificationCases:
  - Add one provider-native field -&gt; its schema, validator, descriptor and CLI/help metadata change without a kernel switch
  - A tree without cancel/option leaves produces no such command or empty parent node
  - A malformed native response is rejected at the adapter boundary before state update
  - A provider capability unavailable due to session is still discoverable with named availability, not falsely Unsupported
  - A pull result or push frame validates independently and never enters order approval/compensation
- openQuestions:
  - Each broker's native idempotency horizon, complete lookup namespaces and absence/fencing proof require real broker evidence; without it retry capability is ReconcileBeforeRetry only.
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: The source fact that UnifiedTradingAccount dispatches through a generic IBroker/global switch is retained as migration evidence, not elevated to target architecture. K01-K03/K07 replace that closed SDK-shaped surface with provider declaration, exact leaf schemas, adapter-native protocols and one fixed UTA-facing boundary; K08 is opt-in for effect leaves.

The final target replaces that as a target requirement with declaration-derived exact leaves, fixed descriptor metadata, adapter-native decoding and optional withTransaction composition; unsupported leaves are absent and availability is separate. The original idempotency/absence question remains empirical-retained, with ReconcileBeforeRetry and Unknown instead of blind retry.

## Cross-group contracts

- All TargetGaps effects use docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/solutions/composition-contract.md K01-K12 as the fixed UTA-facing boundary: providers declare capability leaves and exact input/output/error schemas; provider trees, handlers, languages and native protocols remain open.
- NOTE-2-1 and NOTE-14-1 depend on K02/K06 discovery and transport semantics: capability identity, schema fingerprint, availability, authorization and delivery mode are separate; no universal ActionContractMap or mandatory Unsupported handlers.
- NOTE-2-2, NOTE-8-2, NOTE-8-3, NOTE-8-4 and NOTE-17-1 distinguish K05 pull/push data delivery from K08 controlled effects: data frames/cursors/streams have their own lifecycle, freshness, finality, replay and backpressure; order approval/WAL/compensation apply only when a capability is explicitly wrapped by withTransaction.
- NOTE-4-1, NOTE-5-1, NOTE-5-2, NOTE-7-1, NOTE-7-2 and NOTE-12-1 retain the single local effect authority, writer CAS, durable recovery and lock safety from the investigation, while capability metadata/data projections are typed and scoped rather than forced into the effect state machine.
- NOTE-5-3, NOTE-5-4 and NOTE-5-5 retain exact criterion, compensation, FailurePolicy and Unknown-safe obligations only for composed controlled effects; NativeConformanceRecord remains per provider capability/effect and is not inferred from another adapter.
- NOTE-9-1 is the source-bridge cutover: existing UnifiedTradingAccount/IBroker/global-switch facts remain evidence, but target implementations must compose declaration-derived leaves and fixed UTA-facing descriptors without a kernel broker-name switch or handwritten order Cartesian product.
- NOTE-12-2, NOTE-13-1 and NOTE-16-1 share typed defect/redaction/observability boundaries. Provider protocol/output failures, data gaps and effect OutcomeUnknown are distinct variants and cannot be collapsed into empty results or known rejection.
- NOTE-15-1 and NOTE-18-1 keep simulator/external stimulus provenance separate from UTA effect execution. Real acceptance must traverse authenticated UTA capability/effect paths; data/manual stimulus may test observation only.
- NOTE-18-2 and NOTE-19-1 retain native packaging/home/authority evidence gates. Manifest metadata, SDK method presence, endpoint reachability and mock success never establish native idempotency, absence, atomicity, restoration, ownership or replay guarantees.

- services/uta/src/main.ts:127 and services/uta/src/domain/trading/order-sync-poller.ts:53-105 retain a timer/poller observation path; target implementation must own stop handles and distinguish data stream/cursor lifecycle from controlled-effect scheduler jobs.

- docs/uta-effect-runtime-design/transaction-contract.md §6-7 and architecture lock fields remain controlled-effect evidence only; data delivery leases and cache eviction cannot release economic locks or trigger compensation.
